docs.purpose: Shows a user their own notification inbox, optionally filtered to unread only, and lets them mark one notification or all of their notifications as read.
docs.data_story: It reads 1 table — `notifications` and writes `notifications`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

notes: The header documents a since-fixed IDOR: the handler previously trusted a client-supplied user_id query param and now derives identity only from the verified session. GET uses SELECT * FROM notifications, so the response field surface is unrestricted at the SQL level. No in-repo caller found — the mobile app reads its inbox elsewhere; this route appears unused. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: CENSUS AGREEMENT: census_reads ['notifications'] and census_writes ['notifications'] both match. `SELECT *` at route.ts:46 — columns recorded as "all"; the response therefore leaks any column later added to `notifications` straight to the client. Findings a reviewer must know: (1) three separate round-trips per GET (rows :45, COUNT :53, unread COUNT :66) with the third executed INSIDE the JSON object literal (route.ts:64-72) — it runs even on the unreadOnly=false path only, but the nesting makes the cost invisible; (2) `paramIdx` is a `const` set to 2 (route.ts:37) and the `unreadOnly` branch pushes a literal predicate, not a parameter (route.ts:40) — correct today, but the shape invites an off-by-one if another filter is added; (3) PATCH has no Zod and no JSON try/catch (route.ts:82), so a malformed body is a 500, not a 400; (4) response shapes are bare, not enveloped, despite the withApiEnvelope wrapper (see envelope.deviations). | Idempotency: PATCH is state-convergent, not count-stable. `mark_all_read`: `UPDATE notifications SET is_read = true WHERE user_id = $1 AND is_read = false RETURNING id` (route.ts:87-89) — the `AND is_read = false` predicate IS the guard, so a replay writes zero rows, but the response `{updated: result.length}` (route.ts:92) returns N on the first call and 0 on the replay. `mark_read`: `UPDATE notifications SET is_read = true WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2` (route.ts:97) has NO is_read guard — it re-writes the same value on every replay (no IS DISTINCT FROM), and always answers `{success:true}` (route.ts:100) even when rowCount is 0. | Caching: none observed — no revalidate/dynamic/Cache-Control/unstable_cache in src/app/api/notifications/route.ts:1-104 | Pagination: limit clamped to [1,100] at src/app/api/notifications/route.ts:31 (default 50, NaN->50); offset clamped to [0,100000] at route.ts:33 (default 0, NaN->0). Bound as $2/$3 at route.ts:49-50. ORDER BY created_at DESC (route.ts:48) is not a unique key, so page boundaries can repeat/skip rows sharing a created_at. | Other guards / classification: IDOR fix: every query is bound to the session uid, never a client-supplied user_id (route.ts:35-36, :67, :90, :98; rationale at route.ts:6-11 — comment, not evidence; the evidence is the SQL at those lines). PATCH mark_read is scoped `WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2` (route.ts:97), so a foreign notification_id silently updates 0 rows and still returns `{success:true}` (route.ts:100). | ORPHAN — zero call sites in src/** or mobile/** (sweep 2026-09-15, comment lines stripped). | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.
